articles.title: The Rubber Band Is Real. It Just Isn’t Magic.
articles.dek: Leaders in real NFL and NBA games give back more than team strength explains, and more than a simulated league that ignores the score does. In football it is the last five minutes. In basketball it never stops.

articles.title: Home Court Is Shrinking. Denver Still Has One.
articles.dek: On a straight line through the seasons, NBA home teams won 61.7% of games in 2002 and 55.3% in 2026. The NFL slide could be noise, the empty arenas of 2020-21 took the edge away, and Denver, a mile above sea level, still has the biggest one.

articles.title: The Fresh-Start Myth
articles.dek: We matched 243 NFL trades against similar players who stayed put. The new city barely registered. Players handed a smaller job fell about 3.5 fantasy points a game behind, under every method we tried.

articles.title: Champagne, No Hangover
articles.dek: Champions get worse the year after a title, and so do the teams they most resemble. Across 352 title winners in four leagues, champions in the NBA and NHL, and probably the NFL, fell less far than equally good teams that didn’t win.

articles.title: Payback Is a Rounding Error
articles.dek: Across 1,547 NFL games against a former team, the revenge bump comes to about a third of a fantasy point. Home field is worth about the same.

articles.title: The Cliff
articles.dek: Running backs go over it at 29. Hockey skaters hang on until 32 or later. Both ages come from rebuilding the aging curves for 14 position groups in four leagues, this time counting the players who quietly vanished from the data.
